artists.name: Radiohead
artists.bio: English rock band formed in Abingdon, Oxfordshire in 1985. Over three decades they moved from guitar-driven alternative rock to electronic textures and orchestral arrangements, becoming one of the most influential bands of their era.

artists.name: Boards of Canada
artists.bio: Scottish electronic duo of brothers Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin. Known for warm, degraded analogue synths, nostalgic samples of 1970s educational films, and slow hip-hop influenced rhythms.

artists.name: Daft Punk
artists.bio: French electronic duo Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, formed in Paris in 1993. Pioneers of the French house scene, famous for their robot personas and disco-influenced production.

artists.name: Miles Davis
artists.bio: American jazz trumpeter, bandleader and composer, among the most influential figures in 20th-century music. He was at the forefront of bebop, cool jazz, hard bop, modal jazz and jazz fusion.

artists.name: John Coltrane
artists.bio: American jazz saxophonist and composer. Working in bebop and hard bop early in his career, he helped pioneer modal jazz and later the free jazz movement.

artists.name: Fleetwood Mac
artists.bio: British-American rock band formed in London in 1967. Their 1977 album Rumours is one of the best-selling albums of all time.

artists.name: Kendrick Lamar
artists.bio: Rapper and songwriter from Compton, California, widely regarded as one of the most skilled lyricists of his generation. First rapper outside classical and jazz to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music.

artists.name: Frank Ocean
artists.bio: American singer, songwriter and rapper. Known for an idiosyncratic, unconventional approach to R&B and an intensely private public persona.

artists.name: Bon Iver
artists.bio: American indie folk band founded in 2006 by singer-songwriter Justin Vernon. The debut album was famously recorded in a remote hunting cabin in northwestern Wisconsin.

artists.name: Sufjan Stevens
artists.bio: American singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Detroit. His work ranges from sparse acoustic folk to dense orchestral and electronic arrangements.

artists.name: Massive Attack
artists.bio: English trip hop collective formed in Bristol in 1988. Their dark, cinematic records defined the "Bristol sound" alongside Portishead and Tricky.

artists.name: Portishead
artists.bio: English band formed in Bristol in 1991, named after the nearby coastal town. Combines hip-hop beats, vinyl crackle, film-score samples and Beth Gibbons' haunting vocals.

artists.name: Aphex Twin
artists.bio: Richard D. James, Irish-born British electronic musician. Known for idiosyncratic work spanning ambient, acid and drill and bass, and for his influence on IDM.

artists.name: Brian Eno
artists.bio: English musician, composer and producer, a principal innovator of ambient music. Also known for production work with Talking Heads, U2 and David Bowie.

artists.name: Joni Mitchell
artists.bio: Canadian-American singer-songwriter and painter. Drawing from folk, pop and jazz, she is regarded as one of the most influential songwriters of the 20th century.

artists.name: Tame Impala
artists.bio: Psychedelic music project of Australian multi-instrumentalist Kevin Parker, who writes, records, performs and produces the music almost entirely alone.

artists.name: Beach House
artists.bio: American dream pop duo from Baltimore, Maryland, formed in 2004 by Victoria Legrand and Alex Scally.

artists.name: Mitski
artists.bio: Japanese-American singer-songwriter. Her emotionally raw music moves between indie rock, synth-pop and country-tinged balladry.

artists.name: Phoebe Bridgers
artists.bio: American singer-songwriter from Pasadena, California. Also a member of boygenius with Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus.

artists.name: Japanese Breakfast
artists.bio: Indie pop project of Korean-American musician and author Michelle Zauner, author of the memoir Crying in H Mart.

artists.name: The Beatles
artists.bio: English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960, comprising John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr. The most influential band in the history of popular music.

artists.name: Pink Floyd
artists.bio: English rock band formed in London in 1965, known for philosophical lyrics, sonic experimentation and elaborate live shows.

artists.name: Talking Heads
artists.bio: American new wave band formed in New York City in 1975, fronted by David Byrne. Fused punk, funk, art rock and African polyrhythms.

artists.name: Björk
artists.bio: Icelandic singer, songwriter and producer. Her eclectic catalogue spans electronic, classical, avant-garde and pop.

artists.name: Burial
artists.bio: Anonymous South London producer whose crackling, rain-soaked take on UK garage and 2-step defined a new strand of British electronic music.

artists.name: Kraftwerk
artists.bio: German band formed in Düsseldorf in 1970 by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider. Widely considered innovators and pioneers of electronic music.
